item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports testing temporal relevance and session structure inside a sequential network. “Parameter-Efficiently Leveraging Session Information” (2025) proposes session tokens, session segment embeddings, and temporal self-attention, reporting improvements with little parameter overhead ([paper](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/10902109)). A directly related BERT4Rec extension (June 2026) combines content relevance with continuous-time decay for session attention and learns a gate between long-term and short-term representations ([paper](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44163-026-01554-z)). These findings motivate architectural hypotheses; they do not establish that emphasizing recent interactions improves the pinned Amazon benchmark.\n\nA compatible experiment would add learned time-gap attention biases and content-dependent history relevance within one jointly trained BERT4Rec network. Compare against the unchanged baseline, allowing temporal effects to weaken or reverse rather than imposing monotonic recency decay. Use observed historical timestamps only; no future target timestamp. Preserve reserved-mask target training and appended-mask inference: BERT4Rec’s original Cloze objective specifically prevents target leakage through bidirectional context ([original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690)). Read the appended mask at the final nonpadding position in left-padded sequences. Retain one trained checkpoint per category and select solely by the common macro validation HR@10; published improvements under other datasets and protocols are not transferable guarantees."}
